# Skald

> Skald is web analytics from a website's server log: it counts people, AI assistants and
> crawlers from the requests the server already records, and from an optional script tag.
> This file is for an AI agent that a user asked to set up Skald for their website, or to fix
> a to-do Skald found on it (old pages to redirect, server errors, and the like).

It holds no secret and no code. Skald's own server: __BASE__

## If the user gave you a line with a code

The line has one of three shapes:

- set up Skald for <site> — read this file and use code <code> (a new site: connect its logs,
  add the script tag, and send its leads)
- finish setting up Skald for <site> (<jobs, comma separated>) — read this file and use code
  <code> (only the jobs named, for a site already in Skald: for example "add the script tag",
  "send leads and tool webhooks", "add the Next.js log field", "find the page assets", "check
  the privacy settings", "connect Google Search Console", "connect the AI assistant (MCP)")
- fix the Skald to-do "<title>" for <site> — read this file and use code <code> (one of the
  to-dos on Skald's Overview > Insights; "fix the Skald to-dos for <site> (<n>: "<title>",
  ...)" for several). The steps fetch every row of each to-do from Skald with curl (old
  addresses and the closest live page, Markdown copies AI asks for, server errors by
  address...), find where the site keeps its redirects or rules, change only what is missing,
  and send Skald a report per to-do. Nothing to download, nothing to copy. A "done" report
  marks the to-do done; Skald then checks it on the days after

Each line is for ONE site, with its own code. A user with several sites gets one line per
site and pastes each into the session that works on that site (its own folder, repository or
server). The lines never end each other: several sessions can set up several sites at the
same time. Work only on the site your line names.

Either way:

1. Fetch the site's own steps with curl in a shell, put the code in place of <code>:
   `curl -fsSL __BASE__/traffic-kit/<code>/steps`. Use curl, not a fetch tool: a fetch tool
   may send the address, and so the code, to its provider.
2. Follow those steps in order. They hold only the line's jobs. Each job starts with a check:
   when it is done already, leave it as it is. They say where the keys are, what to change,
   and how to report back.
3. The code works for 24 hours. The keys behind it can be taken once.

## If you are connected to Skald's MCP server

The user may say only "Set up Skald for this site". Then:

1. Call the tool `setup_left`: what is left on the site, and the jobs you can do.
2. Call `setup_line` with those jobs (the token the user connected you with is for this one
   site and has the setup scope; without it, ask the user for a line instead).
3. Follow the line it answers, as below, in this site's own folder or on its server.

"Fix my Skald to-dos": call `fix_todo` (no id: the to-dos you can fix; with an id: every row
and the steps), fix it in the site's code or server as the steps say, then `mark_todo_done`
with the exact change (it needs the setup scope; without it, tell the user what you did).

## If there is no code

Ask the user to make one in Skald: Settings > Sites > Add a site, then pick their AI agent;
for a site already in Skald, a set-up job's "Your AI agent" choice; for several sites,
Settings > Sites > "Set up many sites with your AI agent", which gives each site its own line.
Skald shows a line to paste to you. Do not guess a code.

## Connecting a session to Skald's MCP server (the two lines)

The user makes a token for one site in Skald (Settings > Sites > "Set up many sites with your
AI agent", the site's "Two lines (MCP)") and pastes line 1 into a terminal in that site's own
folder:

- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http skald __BASE__/traffic-mcp --header
  "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` (its default scope keeps it to that folder).
- Codex: a server of its own per site in `~/.codex/config.toml`: `[mcp_servers.skald-<site
  with dashes>]`, `url = "__BASE__/traffic-mcp"`, `http_headers = { Authorization = "Bearer
  <token>" }`.

Line 2 is "Set up Skald for this site". The token goes only into the assistant's settings,
never into a chat message; the user removes it in Settings > AI & API > Tokens & links.

## Rules

1. Never print, echo, log or commit a secret (a token, the lead secret, a tool's secret), and
   never paste one in the chat. Secrets go only in environment variables, the host's secret
   settings, or a file with mode 0600 outside the site's repository.
2. Take the keys only with curl or wget in a shell, straight into a file. Never with a web
   reader or fetch tool: such a tool may pass the page through another model, which would put
   the keys in the chat. Skald refuses it, and the keys stay unused.
3. Never paste the code or the keys anywhere but the commands the steps show: not into
   another chat, a ticket, a commit, or any file in the site's repository.
4. Ask the user before any command that changes a server, and before any change to nginx,
   Apache or another web server's settings. Say what it changes, then wait for a yes.
5. When a fact is missing that you cannot find in the code or on the server, ask the user one
   plain question and wait. Do not guess.
6. Never change a setting in Skald itself: report what you found, and the user applies it.
   At the end, tell the user in plain words what you did, and send the report the steps
   describe.
7. If an answer says "Too many tries", wait a minute and try again.
8. Some things only a person can do, such as giving Skald's robot address access in Google
   Search Console, or copying a Bing API key from Bing's own page. Give the user the exact
   clicks and put them in the report as left for them.
